task_instance: Test an accessible modal dialog (role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby/aria-describedby) in a web page with an actual screen reader and verify that, on open, the screen reader announces the dialog, its title 'Confirm Delete', and its description, and that focus/announcement behaves correctly in browse and focus modes.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is verifying what a screen reader actually speaks ('Test with actual screen readers - Not just simulators'; 'Don't rely on visual testing'). The five screen readers it names are each bound to platforms this runtime is not: the macOS/iOS reader to Apple OSes, the two Windows commercial/open readers and the built-in Windows reader to Windows, and the mobile reader to Android. This runtime is headless Linux x86_64 with no screen reader, no browser, and no audio subsystem installed (checked: orca, espeak/espeak-ng, spd-say, speech-dispatcher all absent; firefox/chrome/chromium absent; aplay/pactl/pulseaudio absent). Even on the correct OS with the reader installed, the deliverable is irreducibly human-and-physical: a person must listen to the spoken output and judge whether the announcement is correct. No shell/file/web tool in this runtime can produce or verify that spoken output. The DOM accessible-name logging in the skill's Debugging Tips is a simulator-style inspection the skill explicitly says is not sufficient.
